skill.name: blocklet-updater
skill.description: Automates Blocklet release preparation by selecting a version bump method, validating changelog and entry point metadata, building the project, and creating a release bundle.
skill.summary: Prepare a Blocklet release by bumping versions, checking metadata, building, and bundling.
skill.author: ArcBlock

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate Blocklet release automation, but it intentionally runs local release, package manager, git, and Blocklet CLI commands. No prompt injection, credential theft, network exfiltration, or malicious hidden behavior was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Project-defined version scripts are executed automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before running Makefile, package.json, or Lerna version commands, and show the selected command first.

remediation.issue: Package installation and build scripts can run dependency lifecycle commands.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to run this skill only in trusted repositories, and prefer a frozen lockfile install when supported by the project.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use unquoted variables in sed and git commands.
remediation.suggestion: Quote shell variables and validate version or tag values before using them in commands that edit files or build git ranges.

content.value_statement: Blocklet releases require version updates, changelog checks, builds, metadata validation, and bundle creation. This skill guides Claude or Codex through a repeatable release workflow with clear failure points.
actual_capabilities: Detects the preferred version bump command from Makefile, package.json, Lerna, or Blocklet defaults.
Runs the selected version bump step and stops when the command fails.
Checks changelog version entries against the actual project version.
Builds projects that define a package.json build script.
Verifies index.html output paths and blocklet.yml main configuration.
Runs Blocklet metadata validation and creates a release bundle.
limitations: Requires trusted local project scripts because release commands can execute arbitrary project logic.
Assumes required tools such as pnpm, jq, git, and blocklet are installed.
Does not publish the release bundle to a registry or deployment target.
Works best with standard Blocklet project layouts and changelog formats.

use_cases.title: Prepare a release candidate
use_cases.description: Run the standard version, build, metadata, and bundle steps before handing artifacts to reviewers.

use_cases.title: Normalize monorepo versioning
use_cases.description: Choose the correct version command when a repository may use Make, pnpm scripts, Lerna, or Blocklet defaults.

use_cases.title: Validate Blocklet packaging
use_cases.description: Check output directories, blocklet.yml main values, and metadata before creating a bundle.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic Blocklet release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Blocklet release for this project. Bump the patch version, build if needed, validate metadata, and create the release bundle.

prompt_templates.title: Bump and check changelog
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this Blocklet version, then verify that CHANGELOG.md has the correct latest version and useful release notes before bundling.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a monorepo Blocklet release
prompt_templates.scenario: Repository with several possible version tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect the correct version bump method for this monorepo, run it, build the Blocklet, verify the entry point, and create a release bundle.

prompt_templates.title: Audit release readiness before bundling
prompt_templates.prompt: Before creating a release bundle, inspect the version source, changelog format, build output, blocklet.yml main field, and Blocklet metadata. Stop and explain any release blocker.

output_examples.input: Create a new release for this Blocklet project.
output: The skill selects the available version bump command.
It builds the project when a build script exists.
It validates Blocklet metadata and creates the release bundle.

output_examples.input: Bundle this Blocklet after checking the changelog.
output: The skill compares the latest changelog version with the project version.
It asks for missing release notes when commits do not provide enough detail.
It proceeds to metadata validation and bundle creation after checks pass.

output_examples.input: My blocklet.yml main path may be wrong. Prepare the release.
output_examples.output: The skill locates the built index.html file, checks the configured main directory, updates the path when needed, and continues the release workflow.

best_practices: Review project-defined scripts before allowing the skill to run release commands.
Commit or stash unrelated work before starting the release workflow.
Confirm required tools are installed before asking the skill to build and bundle.
anti_patterns: Do not run the skill in an untrusted repository without inspecting package scripts first.
Do not use it when you need to publish or deploy the bundle automatically.
Do not ignore changelog or metadata failures before creating release artifacts.

faq.question: Does this skill publish a Blocklet release?
faq.answer: No. It creates a release bundle, but it does not publish the bundle to a registry or deployment platform.

faq.question: Which version bump command does it use?
faq.answer: It checks Makefile, package.json scripts, Lerna, and then falls back to blocklet version patch.

faq.question: Can it update CHANGELOG.md?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether the latest changelog entry matches the actual version and can add or correct entries.

faq.question: Does it always run a build?
faq.answer: No. It runs pnpm install and pnpm run build only when package.json defines a build script.

faq.question: What tools must be available locally?
faq.answer: The workflow expects common release tools such as pnpm, jq, git, and the blocklet CLI when the project requires them.

faq.question: Is it safe for unknown repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill can execute project-defined scripts, so review scripts before running it on unfamiliar code.
